s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain and systemic inflammation with rapid deterioration and multi-organ involvement
salient_findings: Diffuse papules on trunk and extremities
Rapid deterioration requiring intubation and vasopressors
key_facts: Male toddler presented to the emergency department
Abdominal pain and distention of 1 day's duration
Fever and vomiting of 1 day's duration
Bruises on both flanks
Diffuse papules on trunk and extremities developed over 2 days
Condition rapidly deteriorated
Required intubation, vasopressors, and empirical broad-spectrum antibiotics
Hyponatremia and neutropenia present
Elevated liver enzymes (AST: 45 U/L, ALT: 142 U/L)
Elevated C-reactive protein (>270 mg/L) and erythrocyte sedimentation rate (43 mm/h)
Ferritin level: 603 ng/mL
Proteinuria and hematuria on urinalysis
Cavitary lesions in lungs on CT chest/abdomen
Areas of nonenhancement within both kidneys on CT chest/abdomen
Multifocal lesions on MRI brain
Punch biopsy showed small organisms within vasculature and large neutrophilic pustule with inflammation
Tissue Gram staining showed Gram-positive cocci in vessels
Tissue culture, blood culture, bronchial washings, and fluid from bilateral empyemas all showed positive results

shortlist.label: Purpura fulminans
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with purpuric retiform patches, rapid deterioration, and multi-organ involvement, consistent with this condition

shortlist.label: Neisseria meningitidis sepsis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had symptoms of sepsis, including fever, vomiting, and abdominal pain, and laboratory tests showed Gram-positive cocci in vessels

shortlist.label: Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with fever, vomiting, and abdominal pain, and laboratory tests showed elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate

shortlist.label: Meningococcemia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had symptoms of sepsis, including fever, vomiting, and abdominal pain, and laboratory tests showed Gram-positive cocci in vessels

shortlist.label: Staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient presented with fever, vomiting, and abdominal pain, and laboratory tests showed elevated C-reactive protein and erythrocyte sedimentation rate

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with abdominal pain, fever, vomiting, and 'bruises' on both flanks that progressed to purpuric retiform patches, along with laboratory findings of hyponatremia, neutropenia, elevated liver enzymes, and positive tissue culture and Gram staining showing Gram-positive cocci, is most consistent with Purpura fulminans, a condition characterized by rapid progression of hemorrhagic necrosis of the skin and is often associated with severe infections.

rejected.label: Neisseria meningitidis sepsis
rejected.why: While Neisseria meningitidis can cause severe sepsis and purpura, the Gram staining showing Gram-positive cocci does not support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome
rejected.why: Although Streptococcal toxic shock syndrome can present with severe systemic symptoms and skin manifestations, the specific findings of purpuric retiform patches and the laboratory results do not exclusively point to this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Meningococcemia
rejected.why: Meningococcemia typically presents with a petechial or purpuric rash, but the Gram-positive cocci on tissue Gram staining do not align with Neisseria meningitidis, which is Gram-negative.

rejected.label: Staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome
rejected.why: While Staphylococcal toxic shock syndrome can cause severe systemic illness, the presence of purpuric retiform patches and the specific laboratory findings, including the type of organisms seen on Gram stain, are more indicative of Purpura fulminans.

gold: Community-acquired methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (CA-MRSA) sepsis with septic vasculopathy
